findings.scenario: A long-lived MCP process has FTS loaded on database A, then a LOAD attempt on database B fails. Subsequent keyword searches on A return no matches even though its existing pool can still execute FTS queries.
findings.evidence: ExtensionManager stores capability state by extension name only, and markUnavailable overwrites the process-wide fts entry. The pool separately tracks shared.ftsLoaded per Database and reuses unchanged open pools without loading again. This new guard therefore treats B's failure as A's state. An in-memory base/local comparison using the actual registry and search source with a successful A executor returned one match and one executor call at HEAD, but zero matches and zero executor calls with the local diff.
findings.recommendation: Scope the unavailable check to the database/pool being searched, or keep attempting its FTS queries and classify extension-unavailable errors there; do not suppress a pool based on the last process-wide load result.

findings.scenario: The FTS extension loads successfully, but the database has no configured FTS indexes. HTTP /api/search in bm25 mode or hybrid mode without an embedder returns empty results without the missing-index warning or repair guidance.
findings.evidence: The new catch converts the confirmed missing-index Binder exception into []. searchFTSFromLbug's non-pool branch unconditionally increments queriesSucceeded when queryFTS resolves, so it now reports ftsAvailable=true for absent indexes. api.ts only adds ftsDegradedWarning when that flag is false. An in-memory probe executing the base/local queryFTS and search source with the same missing-index exception changed the response from {results:[],ftsAvailable:false} at HEAD to {results:[],ftsAvailable:true} locally. Existing unit tests mock queryFTS and do not exercise this changed catch through the core search branch.
findings.recommendation: Preserve a distinct missing-index outcome through the core adapter and count only successfully executed queries as available. Keep genuine zero-match queries successful and benign missing-index failures out of nonBenignErrors.
